messages:
alex: Heads-up: doing a pass on KV metrics this morning. Found weird divergence between sampled hit-rate and full-scan residency counters for long-lived sessions.
priya: oof, can you share numbers? sampling rate changed anywhere?
alex: sample_rate is the usual 0.01 for telemetry. But when sessions >= 30m, sampled_hit_rate shows +12% vs full-residency estimate. Eviction counters also spike differently.
matt: suspect double-counting during compaction window. We saw compaction tasks emit eviction events and then again as fragment tombstones.
laura: that matches a convo from last week. Need to know whether sampling or event-model is the source. Can you dump a short Profiler trace?
alex: pasted a tiny snippet from perf-runner: `kv_write_path -> compaction -> tombstone_emit` (3.2ms), then `kv_eviction_emit` (0.5ms). compaction emits a counter labeled `eviction_type=\"compaction\"`, eviction emitter increments `eviction_total` with no subtype.
priya: so Prom counters: `kv_evictions_total` (no label), and `kv_evictions_by_type` (compaction/active). The long-session sampler reads `kv_residency_percentile` via periodic job while evictions come from stream. Sampling mismatch.
matt: proposal: normalize sampled hit-rate by effective_sampled_sessions = sampled_sessions * (1 - compaction_fraction) so compaction-driven decrements don't inflate hit-rate.
laura: can you prototype an expression? even a promql-ish hybrid is fine.
alex: rough promql: `sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[5m])) by (model) / max(1, sum(kv_residency_count) by (model))` for raw eviction intensity. For normalized hit: `sum(rate(kv_hits_sampled[5m])) by (model) / sum(rate(kv_lookups_sampled[5m])) by (model) / clamp_min(sample_fraction_adjust, 0.001)` where `sample_fraction_adjust = sampled_sessions / total_estimated_sessions * (1 - compaction_fraction)`
priya: nice. We should also expose a single synthesized metric for dashboards: `kv_effective_pressure` (eCP) = eviction_rate_per_resident * (1 - reuse_rate). Helps rank hot models.
matt: I like eCP. Implementation note: reuse_rate needs to be computed from long-context reuse counters; those are heavy to compute live. Maybe compute reuse_rate in the sampling pipeline batch job and emit as gauge per model once per minute.
laura: dashboard panels I want: 1) eCP over time by model (stacked), 2) residency age heatmap (session age bucket vs residency%), 3) eviction waterfall (compaction vs active vs background), 4) sample health TL;DR (sampled_sessions / estimated_sessions, sample_rate drift).
obs-bot: I created a ticket: infra/obs #452 to add `kv_effective_pressure` and `kv_sample_health` gauges.
alex: thanks obs-bot. Follow-ups: (a) add a small alert when `kv_sample_health < 0.6` for >5m, (b) add note in dashboards about the compaction noise window (annotate last compaction times).
priya: quick check — will this affect any existing alert thresholds? I think `kv_eviction_spike` uses raw evictions; we should change that to use eCP for model-level alerts.
matt: yep. Raw evictions still useful for debugging but model SLOs should be tied to eCP.
laura: ok owners: priya + matt to prototype prom job for normalization, alex to update dashboards, obs-bot will track. Aim for demo in tomorrow's standup.
alex: I'll paste a short sample SQL ETL used in the proto job:```sql
-- compute per-model sampled sessions and compaction fraction
SELECT model,
  sum(sampled_sessions) as sampled_sessions,
  sum(compaction_evictions) / nullif(sum(evictions),0) as compaction_fraction,
  sum(sampled_hits) / nullif(sum(sampled_lookups),1) as sampled_hit_rate
FROM telemetry_extracted
WHERE ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY model;
```
priya: perfect. If the prototype looks good I'll flip the model-level alerts next week.
laura: thanks all — this should make the long-context memory-growth alerts less noisy and give clearer ownership when memory climbs.
alex: ping me if you want the perf traces. I'll attach a flamegraph to the ticket. :thumbsup:
obs-bot: ticket infra/obs #452 updated with label `priority:high` and linked to dashboard PR #89.
